text:
maria: Heads up — staging rollout for model v2.3.0 (ckpt-202603) is blocked. After onboarding the new checkpoint p95 generation latency jumped ~200ms compared to previous canary. Observed across two GPU pools.

jake: Ugh. Is this kernel selection or batching-related? Any CI failures/alerts?

anika: Quick profile shows repeated fallback to a slower matmul path when seq_len > 1024. Also KV cache miss/eviction rate spiked right after the rollout.

ben: Did the tokenizer change with that checkpoint? We had a conversion script earlier that tweaked pad/eos behavior.

maria: Paste of the minimal trace we pulled (staging, 10 requests):

```
# perf_probe snippet
kernel_selection: fused_attention_v2 -> 38% of calls
kernel_selection: matmul_slow -> 49% of calls
kv_cache_hits: 82% -> now 62%
kv_cache_evictions_per_min: 5 -> 120
avg_effective_batch_size: 2.1 -> 1.4
p95_latency_ms: 410 -> 610
```

infra-bot: ci/perf:gen_p95 (staging) failed on run 1975-04; delta +28% — https://ci.redwood/plays/1975-04 (failed tests: gen_p95_threshold).

jake: Plan: bisect the onboard change set. First candidate is the conversion commit that changed tokenizer padding and the model config change that set prefer_fused_attention=false. If reverting either fixes perf we can do a narrow rollback.

anika: Important detail: the conversion pipeline now emits tokenizer config with "eos_trim": true and adds an explicit padding token at the end. That increases average tokenized length for many inputs -> larger KV cache churn and lower batching. Also the model config flag prefer_fused_attention=false will prevent the fused kernel from being chosen even when it's optimal. Together they amplify latency.

maria: Good catch. Two simultaneous deltas (tokenizer padding + kernel hint) could explain the cascade. Workaround options: 1) temporarily force kernel selection override to prefer fused_attention for the model; 2) pin the old tokenizer pad/eos behavior in staging; 3) revert the onboard until we get a clean conversion.

ben: Also check routing: routing policy change yesterday sent more single-turn requests to this pool; avg batch size dropped which magnifies the kernel penalty. Could be a multi-factor failure.

maria: I'll try the kernel override on 2 nodes now (canary) and re-run perf job. If that fixes p95 we can push a hotfix (kernel-hint override). If not, we revert the onboard commit and run a focused bisect.

deploy-bot: scheduled job: apply-kernel-override model=v2.3.0 pool=staging-n2 at 1975004520

maria: Thanks. If anyone sees other correlated changes (routing, autoscale), paste them here. Will follow up with perf numbers in ~15m. :pray:
